headline: 7 top Awami League leaders sent to gallows over July atrocities
summary: Court orders death penalty for seven leaders; assets of four are to be liquidated to compensate July victims.
details: Seven top Awami League leaders have been sentenced to death for their roles in the atrocities committed during the July protests. The verdict comes as a significant development in the legal proceedings regarding the mass violence.
As part of thejudgment, the court has ordered that half of the assets of five leaders be sold. This measure is aimed at providing financial compensation to the victims of the July atrocities.

Specifically, Tk 22.5 crore of the declared assets of four Awami League leaders are set to be liquidated. These funds will be used to support the families and victims of those affected by the violence.
Families of the victims have hailed the verdict as a step toward justice, though many are calling for the swift execution of the sentences to ensure accountability.
The ruling highlights the legal consequences for those found responsible for orchestrating or participating in the July atrocities, marking a critical moment for the victims' families.

headline_marked: Multiple [[cocktail bombs explode in Dhaka]] near DU and Supreme Court
headline: Multiple cocktail bombs explode in Dhaka near DU and Supreme Court
summary: Three explosions occurred near Dhaka University and one in front of the Supreme Court following a death sentence for Awami League leaders.
details: Three cocktail bombs exploded in the Dhaka University area tonight at around 10:45 PM. Two blasts occurred in front of Jagannath Hall and one near the TSC Metro Rail station.
Dhaka University Proctor Israfil Ratan confirmed the incidents, stating that police and assistant proctors have reached the scene to investigate. No casualties have been reported so far.

Earlier today, a cocktail bomb exploded in front of the main gate of the Supreme Court. This happened shortly after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered a death sentence for seven defendants, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the Supreme Court blast was under investigation and two suspects have been identified through CCTV footage.
The Home Minister suggested that the perpetrators could be 'miscreants' from the Awami League and the government is continuing its investigation into the attacks.
caption:
Four cocktail bombs exploded across Dhaka tonight, targeting the Supreme Court and Dhaka University areas.

Earlier today, a cocktail bomb exploded in front of the main gate of the Supreme Court. This happened shortly after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered a death sentence for seven defendants, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the Supreme Court blast was under investigation and two suspects have been identified through CCTV footage.

The Home Minister suggested that the perpetrators could be 'miscreants' from the Awami League and the government is continuing its investigation into the attacks.
